title: CUET Mass Media Test 14
subject: Mass Media / Mass Communication (Code: 318)
syllabus_source: CUET SYLLABUS/Mass Media - 318.pdf (NTA syllabus for CUET (UG) 2026, latest published)
past_paper_reference: Pattern benchmark only: NTA CUET (UG) Mass Media papers 2024, 2025 and 2026, analysed for format only (no questions copied)
textbooks: CBSE Mass Media Studies, Classes XI-XII (curriculum mirrored by the NTA syllabus)
Constitution of India, Articles 19(1)(a) and 19(2); Acts and Supreme Court judgments as cited
Official histories of All India Radio, Doordarshan and Indian cinema
instructions: Each correct answer earns 5 marks; each incorrect answer deducts 1 mark; unattempted questions earn 0.
One set of 5 questions is based on a case; the set stays together.

questions.topic: Radio: writing for radio and radio recording
questions.sub_topic: Why radio is called a blind medium
questions.question: Radio is called a "blind medium" because:
options: A) It uses only sound, with no pictures
B) It cannot be heard by blind people
C) It broadcasts only at night
D) It has no audience at all
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) It uses only sound, with no pictures
Why: Listeners cannot see anything; radio relies on sound alone.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) are false.
Key point: Radio must create pictures in the listener's mind.

questions.topic: Advertising and Public Relations
questions.sub_topic: Who does what in an ad agency
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Role)
(A) Account executive
(B) Copywriter
(C) Art director
(D) Media planner

List-II (Task)
(I) Designs the look and visuals of the ad
(II) Decides which media will carry the ad
(III) Links the agency with the client
(IV) Writes the words of the ad
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
Why: The account executive links agency and client (III). The copywriter writes the words (IV). The art director designs the visuals (I), and the media planner chooses the media (II).
Why not the others: (B) swaps account executive and copywriter. (C) swaps copywriter and art director. (D) swaps art director and media planner.
Key point: An advertisement is the work of a team.

questions.topic: Radio: writing for radio and radio recording
questions.sub_topic: How a microphone picks up sound
questions.question: The pattern showing how sensitive a microphone is to sound from different directions is called its ____.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) polar pattern
Why: A microphone's polar pattern shows the directions from which it picks up sound.
Why not the others: (A) is a range of radio frequencies. (C) is the amount of digital data per second. (D) is music played under speech.
Key point: Choosing the right pattern cuts unwanted noise.

questions.topic: TV Production Process and Programmes
questions.sub_topic: The room where a live show is controlled
questions.question: The room from which the director and crew control a live studio programme is called the ____.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) production control room
Why: The production control room holds the vision mixer, sound desk and monitors used to run the show.
Why not the others: (A) is where guests wait. (C) prepares performers. (D) stores old footage.
Key point: The director calls the shots from the control room.

questions.topic: TV Production Process and Programmes
questions.question:
Arrange the following steps of making a TV documentary in the correct order:
(A) Shoot the footage
(B) Research the subject
(C) Develop the idea
(D) Write the script
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (C), (B), (D), (A)
Why: The team develops the idea, researches it, writes a script, and then shoots.
Why not the others: (A) researches before having an idea. (B) writes the script before research. (D) shoots before the script.
Key point: Good research makes a better script and shoot.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.question:
Arrange the following laws in chronological order:
(A) Indian Press Act
(B) Working Journalists Act
(C) Press and Registration of Books Act
(D) Official Secrets Act
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (C), (A), (D), (B)
Why: The PRB Act came in 1867, the Indian Press Act in 1910, the Official Secrets Act in 1923 and the Working Journalists Act in 1955.
Why not the others: (B) puts 1910 before 1867. (C) puts 1923 before 1910. (D) puts 1955 before 1923.
Key point: Colonial press laws were followed by laws protecting journalists after independence.

questions.topic: TV Production Process and Programmes
questions.question: A TV programme that is broadcast again after its first showing is called a:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Rerun
Why: A rerun is a repeat broadcast of a programme.
Why not the others: (B) is a test episode. (C) and (D) advertise upcoming programmes.
Key point: Reruns fill schedules at low cost.

questions.topic: Radio: writing for radio and radio recording
questions.question: The Prime Minister's radio programme Mann Ki Baat was first broadcast in:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 2014
Why: Mann Ki Baat began on All India Radio in October 2014.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are not the year it began.
Key point: The programme showed that radio still reaches millions.

questions.topic: New Media
questions.sub_topic: Digital images over the real world
questions.question: A phone app that shows digital labels over the live camera view of a street uses:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Augmented reality
Why: Augmented reality places digital images and information over a view of the real world.
Why not the others: (B) carries data as light. (C) is a radio band. (D) designs printed pages.
Key point: Augmented reality blends real and digital worlds.

questions.topic: Cinema: history, production process, genres and cinema for social change
questions.question: The National Film Archive of India, which preserves old Indian films, is located in:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Pune
Why: The National Film Archive of India is in Pune.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) are not where it is located.
Key point: Archives save films that would otherwise be lost.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.question: Kathputli, the string-puppet theatre of Rajasthan, is an example of:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Folk media
Why: Kathputli is a traditional performance form, which makes it a folk medium.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) use technology such as broadcasting, the internet or printing.
Key point: Folk media carry messages in local, trusted forms.

questions.topic: New Media
questions.question: Taking courses and attending classes through the internet is called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) E-learning
Why: E-learning is education delivered online.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) sell products. (D) is online buying and selling.
Key point: New media have expanded access to education.

questions.topic: Advertising and Public Relations
questions.sub_topic: Money set aside for a campaign
questions.question: The total amount of money a company sets aside for its advertising in a year is its advertising ____.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) budget
Why: The advertising budget is the money allotted for advertising.
Why not the others: (A) is a memorable line. (B) is the arrangement of an ad. (C) is the client's instructions.
Key point: The budget decides which media a campaign can afford.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.question: Space on a newspaper page, such as the length of a story or an advertisement, is often measured in ____.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) column centimetres
Why: Newspapers measure space in column centimetres: one column wide and one centimetre deep.
Why not the others: (A) is a video measure. (B) measures image resolution. (D) measures typing or speaking speed.
Key point: Advertising rates are often set per column centimetre.

questions.topic: Advertising and Public Relations
questions.sub_topic: What a PR department does not do
questions.question: A company's PR department handles many jobs. Which of these is NOT one of them?
options: A) Issuing press releases to newspapers
B) Preparing the company's tax returns
C) Organising press conferences for the media
D) Publishing a house journal for staff
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Preparing the company's tax returns
Why: Tax returns are an accounts task, not PR.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are common PR activities.
Key point: PR manages communication with publics.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.question: A doctor uses technical medical terms that the patient does not understand. This is an example of a:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Semantic barrier
Why: Semantic barriers arise when words, such as jargon, are not understood in the same way by both sides.
Why not the others: (A) comes from the surroundings. (B) comes from attitudes or emotions. (C) comes from differing customs.
Key point: Plain language removes semantic barriers.

questions.topic: TV Production Process and Programmes
questions.sub_topic: The shot that sets the scene
questions.question: A wide shot at the start of a scene that shows viewers where the action takes place is called an:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Establishing shot
Why: An establishing shot shows the setting before closer shots follow.
Why not the others: (A) shows a small detail. (B) shows an object close up. (C) is filmed from behind one person.
Key point: Establishing shots orient the viewer.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.sub_topic: The odd one out among four conversations
questions.question: Three of the following are interpersonal communication. Which one is NOT?
options: A) Two friends chatting over tea
B) A doctor talking to a patient
C) A TV news bulletin watched by millions
D) A phone call between a mother and son
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) A TV news bulletin watched by millions
Why: A TV bulletin is mass communication, sent to a large and unknown audience.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) take place between two people.
Key point: Interpersonal communication happens between individuals.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.sub_topic: The paper newspapers are printed on
questions.question: The cheap, thin paper on which newspapers are printed is called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Newsprint
Why: Newsprint is low-cost paper made for printing newspapers.
Why not the others: (A) is glossy paper for magazines. (C) is thick card. (D) is treated animal skin.
Key point: The cost of newsprint is a major expense for newspapers.

questions.topic: Advertising and Public Relations
questions.question: To reach rural buyers, companies often set up stalls and demonstrations at weekly village markets called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Haats
Why: Haats are weekly village markets where many rural people gather.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are mostly urban.
Key point: Rural advertising meets buyers where they gather.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.sub_topic: A task a sub-editor does not do
questions.question: Sub-editors work at the news desk. Which of these jobs is NOT theirs?
options: A) Correcting errors in reporters' copy
B) Writing headlines for the stories on a page
C) Cutting long stories to fit the space
D) Reporting from the scene of an accident
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Reporting from the scene of an accident
Why: Going to the scene is a reporter's job. A sub-editor works at the desk.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are sub-editors' tasks.
Key point: Sub-editors shape raw copy into finished stories.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.question:
Arrange the following Doordarshan programmes in the order in which they were first telecast:
(A) Mahabharat
(B) Chitrahaar
(C) Ramayan
(D) Buniyaad
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (B), (D), (C), (A)
Why: Chitrahaar began in 1982, Buniyaad in 1986, Ramayan in 1987 and Mahabharat in 1988.
Why not the others: (A) puts Buniyaad before Chitrahaar. (C) puts Ramayan before Buniyaad. (D) puts Mahabharat before Ramayan.
Key point: The 1980s were Doordarshan's golden decade.

questions.topic: New Media
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Term)
(A) Bandwidth
(B) Broadband
(C) Wi-Fi
(D) 5G

List-II (Meaning)
(I) A wireless network linking devices in a small area
(II) The fifth generation of mobile networks
(III) An always-on, high-speed internet connection
(IV) The amount of data that can pass in a given time
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
Why: Bandwidth is the data capacity (IV). Broadband is fast, always-on internet (III). Wi-Fi is a local wireless network (I), and 5G is the fifth generation of mobile networks (II).
Why not the others: (A) swaps bandwidth and broadband. (C) swaps broadband and Wi-Fi. (D) swaps Wi-Fi and 5G.
Key point: Faster connections made video-heavy new media possible.

questions.topic: New Media
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about OTT platforms under the IT Rules, 2021:
(A) They must classify content by age, such as U, U/A 7+, U/A 13+, U/A 16+ and A.
(B) They must have a system for handling viewers' complaints.
(C) Every web series needs a CBFC certificate before release.
(D) They must offer parental locks for content rated U/A 13+ and above.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A), (B) and (D) only
Why: (A), (B) and (D) are correct. The rules rely on self-classification and complaint systems.
Why not the others: (C) is false. OTT content does not need CBFC certification. Options (B) and (C) include (C), and (A) leaves out (D).
Key point: OTT platforms regulate themselves under a code of ethics.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.question: A journalist who goes out to gather facts and write news stories is called a:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Reporter
Why: A reporter collects information and writes news stories.
Why not the others: (A) prints the paper. (B) and (C) deliver and sell it.
Key point: Reporters are the newspaper's eyes and ears.

questions.topic: Cinema: history, production process, genres and cinema for social change
questions.sub_topic: Who funds and manages a film
questions.question: The ____ arranges the money for a film and manages its production.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) producer
Why: The producer finances and manages the production.
Why not the others: (A) assembles shots. (B) handles camera and lighting. (C) designs dances.
Key point: Without a producer, a film cannot be made.

questions.topic: Cinema: history, production process, genres and cinema for social change
questions.sub_topic: Four films in order of release
questions.question:
Arrange the following films in order of release:
(A) Sholay
(B) Lagaan
(C) Kaagaz Ke Phool
(D) My Dear Kuttichathan
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (C), (A), (D), (B)
Why: Kaagaz Ke Phool came out in 1959, Sholay in 1975, My Dear Kuttichathan in 1984 and Lagaan in 2001.
Why not the others: (A) puts 1975 before 1959. (C) puts 1984 before 1975. (D) puts 2001 before 1984.
Key point: These films marked firsts in format and reach.

questions.topic: Advertising and Public Relations
questions.sub_topic: A large board beside the road
questions.question: A large outdoor board beside a road that displays advertisements is called a:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Hoarding
Why: A hoarding, or billboard, displays outdoor advertisements.
Why not the others: (A) and (C) are printed handouts. (D) is a short song.
Key point: Hoardings reach people on the move.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) Freedom of the press is not named in the Constitution but is part of the freedom of speech under Article 19(1)(a).
(B) Article 19(2) lists grounds, such as public order and defamation, on which reasonable restrictions may be placed.
(C) The government may restrict the press by executive order, without any law.
(D) Restrictions on free speech must be reasonable.
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (C) only
Why: Only (C) is false. Restrictions under Article 19(2) can be imposed only by law.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are correct. Options (A), (C) and (D) name a correct statement as false.
Key point: Press freedom can be limited only by reasonable restrictions made by law.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.question: Communication that follows official rules and channels, such as a government office's letter to a citizen, is called ____ communication.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) formal
Why: Formal communication follows official channels and set rules.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) are casual and unofficial. (D) takes place within oneself.
Key point: Organisations use both formal and informal communication.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Thinker)
(A) Marshall McLuhan
(B) Jürgen Habermas
(C) Harold Lasswell
(D) David Berlo

List-II (Idea)
(I) Source, message, channel, receiver
(II) The global village
(III) The public sphere
(IV) Who says what, in which channel, to whom, with what effect
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(IV), (D)-(I)
Why: McLuhan spoke of the global village (II). Habermas wrote about the public sphere (III). Lasswell asked "who says what…" (IV), and Berlo gave the SMCR model (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps McLuhan and Habermas. (B) swaps Habermas and Lasswell. (D) swaps Lasswell and Berlo.
Key point: Each thinker explains a different side of communication.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (News agency)
(A) Press Trust of India
(B) Reuters
(C) Associated Press
(D) Agence France-Presse

List-II (Country where it is based)
(I) United Kingdom
(II) United States
(III) France
(IV) India
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(III)
Why: PTI is based in India (IV), Reuters in the United Kingdom (I), AP in the United States (II) and AFP in France (III).
Why not the others: (A) swaps PTI and Reuters. (B) swaps Reuters and AP. (C) swaps AP and AFP.
Key point: News agencies supply stories to papers that cannot cover every place.

questions.topic: Cinema: history, production process, genres and cinema for social change
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) The CBFC certifies films under the Cinematograph Act, 1952.
(B) The 2023 amendment divided the UA category into age-based groups such as UA 7+, UA 13+ and UA 16+.
(C) An "A" film may be shown to anyone above 12 years of age.
(D) An "S" film is meant for a specialised audience, such as doctors.
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (C) only
Why: Only (C) is false. An "A" film is restricted to adults, that is, those aged 18 and above.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are correct. Options (B), (C) and (D) name a correct statement as false.
Key point: Certification guides viewers on a film's suitability.

questions.topic: Advertising and Public Relations
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) PR professionals should not offer gifts or money to journalists for coverage.
(B) PR professionals should make clear whom they represent.
(C) Spreading false information is acceptable if it protects the client.
(D) The Public Relations Society of India has a code of ethics for its members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A), (B) and (D) only
Why: (A), (B) and (D) are correct. Ethical PR is honest and open about its clients.
Why not the others: (C) is false. Lying destroys trust and breaks every PR code. Options (B) and (D) include (C), and (A) leaves out (D).
Key point: Credibility is the main asset of public relations.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.sub_topic: Telling soft news from hard news
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of soft news?
options: A) A report on the Union Budget announced today
B) A feature on a street artist who paints city walls
C) A report on a train accident this morning
D) Results of state elections declared today
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) A feature on a street artist who paints city walls
Why: Soft news is human-interest material that is not urgent, such as a feature on an artist.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are hard news that must be reported at once.
Key point: Soft news is about interest; hard news is about urgency.

questions.topic: Radio: writing for radio and radio recording
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about community radio in India:
(A) Community radio stations are run by non-profit groups and educational institutions.
(B) They serve a small local area.
(C) They are owned and run by large commercial companies.
(D) Anna FM, started by Anna University in 2004, is regarded as the first campus community radio station.
Which of the statements given above is/are NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (C) only
Why: Only (C) is false. Community radio is non-commercial and run by the community, not by large companies.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are correct. Options (A), (B) and (C) name a correct statement as false.
Key point: Community radio gives local people a voice of their own.

questions.topic: Cinema: history, production process, genres and cinema for social change
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Festival)
(A) Cannes Film Festival
(B) Berlin International Film Festival
(C) Venice Film Festival
(D) International Film Festival of India

List-II (Where it is held)
(I) Germany
(II) Italy; it is the oldest film festival
(III) France
(IV) Goa, India
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(IV)
Why: Cannes is in France (III), the Berlinale in Germany (I) and Venice, the oldest festival, in Italy (II). IFFI is held in Goa (IV).
Why not the others: (A) swaps Cannes and Berlin. (B) swaps Berlin and Venice. (C) swaps Venice and IFFI.
Key point: Festivals give films international exposure.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.sub_topic: Raja Ram Mohan Roy's Bengali weekly
questions.question: Raja Ram Mohan Roy started the Bengali weekly ____ in 1821.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Sambad Kaumudi
Why: Sambad Kaumudi, started by Ram Mohan Roy, campaigned for social reform.
Why not the others: (B) began in 1868. (C) was a Hindi paper of 1826. (D) was a Gujarati paper.
Key point: Early Indian papers were tools of social reform.

questions.topic: Cinema: history, production process, genres and cinema for social change
questions.sub_topic: The main character of a story
questions.question: The main character of a film, around whom the story is built, is called the:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Protagonist
Why: The protagonist is the central character.
Why not the others: (A) appears in the background. (B) tells the story. (D) reviews films.
Key point: Stories follow the protagonist's goals and struggles.

questions.topic: Radio: writing for radio and radio recording
questions.sub_topic: People who run a radio station
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Role)
(A) Station director
(B) Producer
(C) Sound engineer
(D) Radio jockey

List-II (Task)
(I) Presents shows and talks to listeners
(II) Heads the station
(III) Looks after equipment and sound quality
(IV) Plans and puts together programmes
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(III), (D)-(I)
Why: The station director heads the station (II). The producer plans programmes (IV). The sound engineer handles equipment (III), and the radio jockey presents shows (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps director and producer. (B) swaps producer and engineer. (D) swaps engineer and radio jockey.
Key point: A radio station needs editorial, technical and on-air staff.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.question: Smiling at a friend to show that you are happy to see them is an example of:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Non-verbal communication
Why: A smile sends a message without words.
Why not the others: (B) and (D) use words. (C) reaches large audiences through media.
Key point: Facial expressions are a powerful form of non-verbal communication.

questions.topic: TV Production Process and Programmes
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Graphic)
(A) Ticker
(B) Channel logo (bug)
(C) Full-screen graphic
(D) Split screen

List-II (Description)
(I) A line of text scrolling at the bottom of the screen
(II) Figures or a chart filling the whole screen
(III) Two pictures shown side by side
(IV) A small channel mark in a corner of the screen
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(I), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(III)
Why: A ticker scrolls text (I). A bug is the channel's corner mark (IV). A full-screen graphic shows figures (II), and a split screen shows two pictures (III).
Why not the others: (A) swaps ticker and bug. (C) swaps bug and full-screen graphic. (D) swaps full-screen graphic and split screen.
Key point: Graphics add information to the picture.

questions.topic: Advertising and Public Relations
questions.question: Coordinating advertising, PR, sales promotion and digital media so that they all send one consistent message is called:
options: B) Bulk media buying and planning
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Integrated marketing communication
Why: Integrated marketing communication makes all promotional tools work together.
Why not the others: (A) promotes banned products indirectly. (B) purchases space and time. (C) hides the advertisement.
Key point: Consistency strengthens a brand.

questions.topic: Communication: levels, models, culture, social change and the evolution of media
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) Kinesics is the study of body movements and gestures.
(B) Proxemics is the study of how people use space.
(C) Paralanguage refers to the tone, pitch and pace of the voice.
(D) Haptics is the study of how people use time.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A), (B) and (C) are correct.
Why not the others: (D) is false. Haptics is the study of touch; the use of time is chronemics. Options (B) and (C) include (D), and (A) leaves out (C).
Key point: Much meaning travels without words.

questions.topic: Journalism: news, the journalist, reporting and editing, photojournalism, media laws and ethics
questions.sub_topic: Secret information passed to a reporter
questions.question: Confidential official information deliberately passed to a journalist by an insider is called a:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Leak
Why: A leak is secret information given to the press without official approval.
Why not the others: (B) is the first paragraph. (C) labels a story. (D) is a page plan.
Key point: Journalists must check leaked material before using it.

questions.topic: Social Media
questions.question:
Read the following case and answer the question that follows.

For years, trucks had been dumping construction debris into Kalyani Lake on the edge of a small town. One evening a college student posted photos of the shrinking lake with the hashtag #SaveKalyaniLake. Within days, a short video of dead fish on the shore had been shared thousands of times, and many residents changed their profile pictures to a drawing of the lake. An online petition to the municipal corporation gathered 40,000 signatures. Through WhatsApp groups, volunteers organised a weekend clean-up that drew 600 people.

At the height of the campaign, a message began circulating that claimed the lake would be "sold to a builder tomorrow". It carried an image of an official-looking government order. Before reacting, the admins of the main groups checked with the municipal office and a fact-checking website. They found that the order had been doctored, and posted a correction asking members not to forward the message.

A month later, the corporation announced fencing around the lake and an inquiry into the dumping. Some critics still described the online support as "slacktivism", saying that liking a post costs nothing.

Question: The #SaveKalyaniLake campaign is best described as an example of:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Cyber activism
Why: Cyber activism uses the internet and social media to raise awareness and push for change.
Why not the others: (B) is harassment of a person. (C) is a paid commercial message. (D) is misuse of someone's personal details.
Key point: Social media let ordinary citizens start public campaigns.

Question: Residents using the same hashtag and changing their profile pictures to a drawing of the lake shows that the campaign:
options: A) Was secretly paid for by a political party
B) Built a shared sense of collective identity
C) Was meant mainly to sell lake-themed products
D) Had stopped spreading beyond the college
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Built a shared sense of collective identity
Why: Shared symbols, such as a hashtag and matching pictures, make people feel part of one group with one cause.
Why not the others: (A) and (C) have no basis in the case. (D) is wrong; the campaign spread across the town.
Key point: Hashtags help scattered people see themselves as one movement.

Question: What did the group admins do right when the message about the lake's sale appeared?
options: A) Forwarded it at once so that everyone was warned
B) Deleted the groups to stop all discussion
C) Checked official sources before posting a correction
D) Added their own comments and shared it widely

Question: Which feature of the campaign most likely pushed the corporation to act?
options: A) The large number of likes on the first photo
B) The fake order that spread at the campaign's peak
C) The critics who called the campaign slacktivism
D) Online support turning into a petition and a clean-up
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Online support turning into a petition and a clean-up

Why not the others: (A) alone is weak pressure. (B) could have harmed the campaign. (C) criticised it.

An online petition to the municipal corporation gathered 40,000 signatures. Through WhatsApp groups, volunteers organised a weekend clean-up that drew 600 people.

A month later, the corporation announced fencing around the lake and an inquiry into the dumping. Some critics still described the online support as "slacktivism", saying that liking a post costs nothing.

Question: Which fact from the case best answers the critics who called the campaign "slacktivism"?
options: A) Six hundred people turned up for the clean-up organised online
B) Many residents changed their profile pictures to the lake
C) The video of dead fish was shared thousands of times
D) A doctored government order circulated in the groups
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Six hundred people turned up for the clean-up organised online
Why: Slacktivism means low-effort online support. A clean-up that drew 600 people shows that online support led to real effort.
Why not the others: (B) and (C) are the low-effort actions the critics meant. (D) does not show any real effort.
Key point: Real-world action is the best answer to the slacktivism charge.
